raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Summary:
Load an initial Hugging Face safetensors checkpoint (`checkpoint.initial_load_in_hf`) through a temporary, model-only `torch_checkpointing` manager.

The model state is converted with the state-dict adapter (`to_hf`), loaded in place, and restored with `from_hf`. The load names the export's format with `metadata_format=HuggingFaceSafetensorsDistributedMetadataFormat`: an export has no native metadata, and `torch_checkpointing` only reads a non-native format the caller names. The model item keeps its `DefaultResharder`, which reshards every safetensors source into the model's DTensors. The temporary manager loads the export as the `model` item, so `torch_checkpointing` reads `model.safetensors.index.json` or `model.safetensors`, and the probe checks those two names, with no directory listing. Exports named after another item, such as diffusers' `diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json` for Flux, are left as a TODO for a follow-up. Retention's validity check uses `model`, the name this checkpointer writes its own exports under. The load is `strict`, but only over the weights `to_hf` maps, so parameters an export does not carry, such as new LoRA adapters, keep their initialized values. A native base checkpoint cannot yet initialize a LoRA model, since its strict load requires the adapter parameters; a TODO marks that. Quantized Hugging Face loads are rejected for now.

It also imports `METADATA_FILE_NAME` from `torch_checkpointing.metadata_serialization`, where it now lives.

Every `torch_checkpointing` API it uses, including `metadata_format`, `torch_checkpointing.hf.metadata` and `METADATA_FILE_NAME` in `metadata_serialization`, is on `torch_checkpointing` main. The probe spells the single-file name, `{item_key}.safetensors`, itself.

Test Plan:
Against `torch_checkpointing` main:
```
pytest -q tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_torch_checkpointing.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_state_dict_adapter.py
pre-commit run --files torchtitan/components/checkpointer/torch_checkpointing.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_torch_checkpointing.py
```
55 passed, 24 subtests passed. `test_hf_load_reads_a_real_safetensors_export` loads a real indexed `model` export into an `nn.Linear` with no mocks, and `test_hf_load_leaves_parameters_the_export_does_not_carry` loads one into a model with an extra LoRA-like parameter, which keeps its value; loading the export by plain path instead fails with "Missing files for checkpoint items ['model']". pre-commit: clean. Repo-wide pyrefly reports no `torch_checkpointing` errors.

nodes.body:
The PR summary mentions `HFSafetensorsDTensorResharder`. But here we use DefaultResharder. Which one is correct?

From Agent:
```
Without metadata.pkl, DefaultResharder is skipped. With layout=None, the backend uses
its native filename and tries to open:

hf_checkpoint/model_0.pt

I reproduced this with a real model.safetensors file. The load failed with:

RuntimeError: Missing file .../hf/model_0.pt for key model.
```
Curious, do we need to hard code this value?
Is this for saving and loading timeout?

The probe only accepts model.safetensors*, while FluxStateDictAdapter supports diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json. Flux loading fails before the metadata reader runs. Detect supported safetensors files without hard-coding only the model prefix.

Let's add a TODO for Flux.
Curious, who define this model_spec? Are users ever going to change the spec?
We need to expose this. LoRA training will only read the base model checkpoint from hf checkpoint but some parameters are new.
Or at least add a TODO in case we forget.

No, we don't.  @ivy-zhou can you move titan over to use `DefaultStoreBarrier` instead of `TCPStoreBarrier`?  In prod jobs, the default store is a `TCPStore` so it have equivalent performance without the overhead of setting up and connecting to a second store.  Might need to modify tests if any are running in a situation where a default store hasn't been configured.

This is for saving -- it's how long the background write is allowed to go before it errors.  

On the load side there is no collectives/coordination, so no barrier use.
This is currently a limitation in in the current impl of torch_checkpointing -- it's hard-coded to `model` there.
Sounds good, I wrote this before you wrote DefaultStoreBarrier. Let's do this in a separate PR, added here: https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5170

I was looking into this this morning, basically DCPv1 doesn't read the index atm, it just reads every .safetensors file and builds the header information from there. I added a way (in a separate PR) to get this information of "diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json" into the torch_checkpointing side by inferring it from the model key, i.e. Titan can pass us {"diffusion_pytorch_model": model_state} and we can load into it. What do folks think?

I removed it, this is just talking about the fact that HF export doesn't have the metadata.pkl file that we are expecting from a torch_checkpointing checkpoint (metadata.pkl is the "native metadata"). There's no logic in torch_checkpointing to try to probe for some HF specific index files, that's what it means by "the backend never detects one from a plain path". I think this is more confusing than it helps haha

Trainer defines the ItemSpec of each item, and it has to do with the nature of the item itself. For example `item_spec.requires_copy` is for requiring staging copy of the optimizer and model, because the model is going to mutate those and we don't want the checkpoint write and the model writes to race.
Sounds good, I think we need a separate PR, talked to Claude about this and it said we don't have support for this in the DCPv1 side load either
Thanks, we need to wait for torch_checkpointing diffs landed first before landing this PR, is this correct? Or did you land all the depended diffs?
I double check with @jinsooihm, currently state_dict adapter will remove LoRA states. So we are good now. But we need to think about how to better support LoRA states saving and loading. Not urget.

inline_comments.body:
The PR summary mentions `HFSafetensorsDTensorResharder`. But here we use DefaultResharder. Which one is correct?

From Agent:
```
Without metadata.pkl, DefaultResharder is skipped. With layout=None, the backend uses
its native filename and tries to open:

hf_checkpoint/model_0.pt

I reproduced this with a real model.safetensors file. The load failed with:

RuntimeError: Missing file .../hf/model_0.pt for key model.
```
Curious, do we need to hard code this value?
Is this for saving and loading timeout?

The probe only accepts model.safetensors*, while FluxStateDictAdapter supports diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json. Flux loading fails before the metadata reader runs. Detect supported safetensors files without hard-coding only the model prefix.

Let's add a TODO for Flux.
Curious, who define this model_spec? Are users ever going to change the spec?
We need to expose this. LoRA training will only read the base model checkpoint from hf checkpoint but some parameters are new.
Or at least add a TODO in case we forget.

No, we don't.  @ivy-zhou can you move titan over to use `DefaultStoreBarrier` instead of `TCPStoreBarrier`?  In prod jobs, the default store is a `TCPStore` so it have equivalent performance without the overhead of setting up and connecting to a second store.  Might need to modify tests if any are running in a situation where a default store hasn't been configured.

This is for saving -- it's how long the background write is allowed to go before it errors.  

On the load side there is no collectives/coordination, so no barrier use.
This is currently a limitation in in the current impl of torch_checkpointing -- it's hard-coded to `model` there.
Sounds good, I wrote this before you wrote DefaultStoreBarrier. Let's do this in a separate PR, added here: https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5170

I was looking into this this morning, basically DCPv1 doesn't read the index atm, it just reads every .safetensors file and builds the header information from there. I added a way (in a separate PR) to get this information of "diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json" into the torch_checkpointing side by inferring it from the model key, i.e. Titan can pass us {"diffusion_pytorch_model": model_state} and we can load into it. What do folks think?

I removed it, this is just talking about the fact that HF export doesn't have the metadata.pkl file that we are expecting from a torch_checkpointing checkpoint (metadata.pkl is the "native metadata"). There's no logic in torch_checkpointing to try to probe for some HF specific index files, that's what it means by "the backend never detects one from a plain path". I think this is more confusing than it helps haha

Trainer defines the ItemSpec of each item, and it has to do with the nature of the item itself. For example `item_spec.requires_copy` is for requiring staging copy of the optimizer and model, because the model is going to mutate those and we don't want the checkpoint write and the model writes to race.
Sounds good, I think we need a separate PR, talked to Claude about this and it said we don't have support for this in the DCPv1 side load either
I double check with @jinsooihm, currently state_dict adapter will remove LoRA states. So we are good now. But we need to think about how to better support LoRA states saving and loading. Not urget.
